h: Finding an End and a Hope Within Exile

p: "It does not say 'He will bring back,'
כִּי אִם וְשָׁב וְקִבֶּץ (דְּבָרִים ל, ג)
but rather 'He will return and gather'" (Devarim 30:3):
Hashem Yisbarach wrote, as it were,
מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׁב עִמָּהֶן
"This teaches that HaKadosh Baruch Hu returns with them
וּבַפְּסִיקְתָּא (חֲדָשָׁה סִימָן צז) (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא טז, ט)
And in the Pesikta (Chadasha, siman 97) (Pesikta deRav Kahana 16:9):
"It is like a king who had a palace, etc.,
the palace or the owner of the palace?
Is it not the owner of the palace? Etc.
It is like a king who had a vineyard,
the vineyard or the owner of the vineyard?
כִּי כֶרֶם ה׳ צְבָאוֹת וְגוֹמֵר (יְשַׁעְיָה ה, ז)
'For the vineyard of Hashem of Hosts,' etc. (Yeshayahu 5:7).
It is like a king who had a flock,
the flock or the owner of the flock? Etc.
comfort Me, comfort Me, My people," etc.
which enemies came and burned down;
and the parable of the vineyard
"For from Tziyon will go forth Torah,
and the word of Hashem from Yerushalayim";
and they were exiled from Tziyon and from Yerushalayim.
That is why the parable says
And it says that one must console
the owner of the palace, the owner of the vineyard
and the owner of the flock.
the consolations were said only to Yisrael:
דַּבְּרוּ עַל לֵב יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְגוֹמֵר (יְשַׁעְיָה מ, ב)
"Speak to the heart of Yerushalayim," etc. (Yeshayahu 40:2),
But since Yisrael will be consoled
meaning that willful sins become like merits,
and the exile is only for the good
אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי חוֹשֵׁב עֲלֵיכֶם נְאוּם ה׳
that I think concerning you, says Hashem,
thoughts of peace and not of evil,
to give you an end and a hope."
that one sees the good explicitly,
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יד, ב)
similar to what they said (Bava Basra 14b):
but a calamity that has a good end,"
for they saw that Dovid came out of it.
So too, right away in the Babylonian exile,
they saw that Torah she'b'al peh spread
more than You decreed upon me," etc.;
came from the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah.
וְשָׁם הָיָה הֶחָרָשׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר אָלֶף (מְלָכִים ב כד, טז)
And there were "the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand" (Melachim II 24:16),
וְלֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶם אֱדוֹם וְיָוָן וְכוּלֵּי
and over which Edom and Yavan did not rule, etc.
the light that was created on the first day, etc.
and this they saw explicitly in Bavel.
This is the meaning of the word "end."
וְזֶה שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ עַל זֶה (תַּעֲנִית כט, ב)
This is why it is expounded on this (Taanis 29b):
"These are date palms and linen garments,"
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh;
for in Bavel there were date palms,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים פח, רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)
So that they would eat dates
for they were distinguished by their garments (Shabbos 145b),
that is, in white linen garments,
וְרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה אָמַר
And our holy Rebbe, zecher tzaddik livrachah, said
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
And date palms allude to this,
for it is the last species
"And a hope" refers to the future,
שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
for I heard from our holy Rebbe, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
that he said in the name of the Rebbe Reb Bunim,
who said that although in the generations
yet the point of life in the heart
that this was a new thing to him
when he heard it in Peshischa,
and afterward he found the matter stated explicitly
but he did not explain to us where they are.
We have already given the root of this
and this is the good hope in the exile.
This is why Hashem Yisbarach says,
the end and the good hope.
"Speak to the heart of Yerushalayim," etc.:
recognizing that the exiles are for the good,
to give them an end and a hope.
And so, of itself, there is consolation
for the owner of the vineyard, the owner of the flock
and the owner of the palace,
that everything is for the good:
in order to merit the light of Mashiach
that will be revealed through him;
and the lengthening of the exiles
is so that all the souls be rectified,
as at the close of the haftarah (Yeshayahu 40:26):
